examples.ko: 오늘 졸업식 식순을 미리 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me today's graduation ceremony program in advance.
Following the program, we will start with the pledge to the flag.
The program changed, so the congratulatory speech comes first.
They handed out the event program sheet at the entrance.
The host is running the event while looking at the program.
Wouldn't it be boring if the program is too long?

explain: '순서'는 어떤 일에든 쓰지만 '식순'은 졸업식, 개회식 같은 공식 행사의 진행 순서에만 써요. '식순에 따라', '식순을 짜다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: '순서' (order) can be used for anything, but '식순' is only for the running order of formal ceremonies such as graduations or opening events. You will hear it in phrases like '식순에 따라' and '식순을 짜다'.

examples.en: After finishing the run, I panted for a long while.
My angry younger sibling is huffing in the room.
Why are you walking over huffing like that?
I ran up the stairs and am breathing hard.
I can hear a cow snorting over there.

examples.ko: 그는 분이 안 풀려서 식식거리며 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: He was still angry and sat there breathing roughly.

explain: 숨을 거칠게 쉬는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이라서 화가 났거나 숨이 찰 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '씩씩거리다'를 더 자주 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound of rough breathing, so it is used when someone is angry or out of breath. You will hear '씩씩거리다' with the same meaning more often.

examples.en: He was so sunk in grief that he stopped eating and drinking altogether.
For days I forgot to eat and drink and just worked.

examples.ko: 할머니는 병이 나신 뒤로 식음을 거의 못 하세요.
examples.en: Since she fell ill, Grandmother can hardly eat or drink.

examples.ko: 식음도 잊을 만큼 게임에 푹 빠졌어요.
examples.en: I was so into the game that I even forgot to eat and drink.

examples.ko: 충격이 컸는지 식음을 끊고 누워만 있어요.
examples.en: Maybe the shock was big; she has stopped eating and drinking and just lies down.

examples.ko: 시험 결과를 기다리느라 식음을 전폐하다시피 했어요.
examples.en: While waiting for the exam results, I all but stopped eating and drinking.

explain: '먹고 마시는 것'을 한 단어로 묶은 말이라 일상 대화보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 많이 보여요. 주로 '식음을 전폐하다'처럼 걱정이나 슬픔 때문에 못 먹는 상황에 써요.

phrases.example: 아들 소식을 듣고 어머니는 식음을 전폐하셨어요.
phrases.en: Hearing the news about her son, his mother refused all food and drink.
phrases.nuance_ko: 슬픔이나 충격 때문에 아무것도 먹고 마시지 않는다는 굳은 표현이에요. 좀 무겁고 글 같은 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fixed expression for not eating or drinking anything because of grief or shock. It sounds heavy and bookish.

explain_en: It bundles eating and drinking into one word, so you see it more in writing and the news than in casual talk. It is mostly used in '식음을 전폐하다' when worry or grief stops someone from eating.

examples.en: I'm going to take my physical exam next month.
I got a grade 3 result at the physical exam.
The date for the physical exam came out, so I took a day off.
My older brother went to the hospital because of his physical exam.

examples.ko: 신검을 받기 전에 밥을 먹지 말래요.
examples.en: They say not to eat before the physical exam.

examples.ko: 친구는 신검 결과가 좋아서 현역으로 가요.
examples.en: My friend's physical exam result was good, so he is going to active duty.

explain: '신체검사'의 줄임말로, 주로 군대에 가기 전에 받는 검사를 말할 때 써요. 학교나 회사의 건강검진에는 보통 '건강검진'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is short for '신체검사' and is mostly used for the exam taken before military service. For school or work checkups people usually say '건강검진'.

examples.en: The nervous system sends signals throughout the whole body.
We learned about the nervous system in science class.

examples.ko: 이 병은 신경계에 문제가 생겨서 걸려요.
examples.en: This disease comes from a problem in the nervous system.

examples.ko: 잠을 못 자면 신경계가 약해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you can't sleep, your nervous system can weaken.

examples.ko: 신경계 그림을 보고 이름을 써 보세요.
examples.en: Look at the nervous system diagram and write the names.
The central nervous system consists of the brain and spinal cord.

explain: '계'가 붙은 '소화계', '순환계'처럼 몸의 한 체계를 가리켜요. '중추 신경계', '말초 신경계'처럼 나눠 말하는 경우가 많고, 수업이나 건강 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Like '소화계' (digestive system) and '순환계' (circulatory system), the '계' ending names a body system. It is often divided into '중추 신경계' and '말초 신경계', and shows up in classes and health talk.

examples.en: These days I'm suffering from nervous gastritis.

examples.ko: 신경성 두통이라서 약이 잘 안 들어요.
examples.en: It's a stress-related headache, so medicine doesn't work well.
The doctor said it was stress-related.
Every exam I get a nervous stomachache.

examples.ko: 신경성 소화불량에는 잠을 푹 자는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: For nervous indigestion, it's good to get plenty of sleep.
These symptoms are quite likely stress-related.

explain: 뒤에 병 이름이나 증상을 붙여 '신경성 위염', '신경성 두통'처럼 써요. 몸에 큰 이상이 있어서가 아니라 스트레스나 마음의 긴장이 원인일 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It goes before an illness or symptom, as in '신경성 위염' or '신경성 두통'. It is used when the cause is stress or mental tension rather than a clear physical problem.

examples.en: This invention opened a new era in medicine.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 한국 영화사에 신기원을 이뤘어요.
examples.en: That film marked a new epoch in Korean film history.
The arrival of the internet was a new era for communication.

examples.ko: 이번 탐사는 우주 개발의 신기원이 될 거예요.
examples.en: This exploration will become a new epoch in space development.

examples.ko: 이 작품은 신기원을 연 소설로 평가받아요.
examples.en: This work is regarded as a novel that started a new era.

examples.ko: 새 기술이 산업의 신기원을 가져올 거예요.
examples.en: The new technology will bring a new epoch to the industry.

explain: '새 시대'처럼 이전과 확실히 달라지는 출발점을 크게 말할 때 써요. '신기원을 열다', '신기원을 이루다'처럼 쓰고, 일상 대화보다 기사나 글에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It marks a clear starting point that is very different from what came before, like a 'new era'. It is used in '신기원을 열다' and '신기원을 이루다', and appears more in articles and writing than in daily talk.

en: be possessed by a spiritual presence

examples.en: That actor acted as if possessed.

examples.ko: 무대 위의 가수가 신들린 것 같았어요.
examples.en: The singer on stage seemed to be possessed.
I drew all night like someone possessed.

examples.ko: 저 사람은 뭔가에 신들렸는지 갑자기 말이 달라졌어요.
examples.en: Maybe he's possessed by something; his way of talking suddenly changed.
Everyone applauded the almost supernatural hand movements.

examples.ko: 피아노를 치는 그녀는 신들린 사람 같아요.
examples.en: She looks possessed when she plays the piano.

explain: '신이 들리다'가 줄어든 말이에요. 실제 무속 이야기도 되지만, 요즘은 '신들린 듯'처럼 믿기 어려울 만큼 몰입해서 잘한다는 칭찬으로 더 많이 들어요.

phrases.en: The pianist played as if possessed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진짜 귀신이 들린 게 아니라 놀랄 만큼 몰입해서 잘한다는 칭찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not mean real possession; it praises someone for being so absorbed that they perform amazingly.

explain_en: It comes from '신이 들리다'. It can refer to real spirit possession, but these days you mostly hear '신들린 듯' as praise for doing something amazingly well while totally absorbed.

examples.en: When May came, the mountains filled with fresh green.
I walked along a forest path thick with fresh greenery.

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤라 신록이 더 싱그러워요.
examples.en: It rained, so the fresh green looks even more vibrant.
Looking at the fresh green outside the window calms my mind.
I want to travel in the season of fresh green leaves.
In every park the fresh green shines dazzlingly.

explain: 봄이 끝나고 초여름으로 가며 새로 난 잎이 푸르게 올라온 모습을 말해요. 가을의 '단풍'과 짝처럼 계절 느낌을 줘서 글이나 인사말에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It describes the fresh new leaves turning bright green as spring moves into early summer. It pairs in feeling with autumn's '단풍' and often appears in writing and seasonal greetings.

examples.en: That teacher is held in deep trust by the students.
He is an honest person, so he earned people's trust.
His lie came out and he lost people's trust.
The team leader is highly respected and trusted among colleagues.

examples.ko: 신망을 쌓으려면 약속을 잘 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: To build trust, you have to keep your promises.

examples.ko: 그는 지역 주민의 신망을 한 몸에 받고 있어요.
examples.en: He enjoys the full trust of the local residents.

explain: '신뢰'가 일반적인 믿음이라면 '신망'은 사람들이 어떤 사람을 믿고 우러러보는 평판에 가까워요. '신망이 두텁다', '신망을 얻다/잃다'처럼 정해진 짝으로 많이 써요.
explain_en: While '신뢰' is trust in general, '신망' is closer to the reputation of being trusted and looked up to. It is used in set pairings like '신망이 두텁다' and '신망을 얻다/잃다'.

examples.en: After the ports opened, new foreign goods and ideas came in quickly.
He was a person very interested in new foreign things.
The speed of accepting new things differed by country.
At the museum I saw an exhibit introducing new imported things.
People at the time found the new things amazing.
Western innovations changed daily life a lot.

explain: 주로 역사 이야기에서 새로 들어온 외국의 기술, 제도, 물건을 가리켜요. 요즘 나온 신제품에는 잘 쓰지 않고, '신문물을 받아들이다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in history talk for newly arrived foreign technology, systems and goods. It is not used for today's new products; a typical phrase is '신문물을 받아들이다'.

examples.en: In the Joseon era, the class system was strict.
As the status system disappeared, society changed.
We discussed the status system in history class.

examples.ko: 신분제 때문에 능력이 있어도 벼슬을 못 했어요.
examples.en: Because of the status system, people couldn't hold office even if they were capable.

examples.ko: 그 소설은 신분제의 문제를 보여 줘요.
examples.en: That novel shows the problems of the status system.
Voices calling to abolish the status system grew louder.

explain: 태어난 신분에 따라 사람의 지위가 정해지는 제도를 말해서 주로 역사 수업과 역사 드라마 이야기에 나와요. '신분제를 폐지하다', '신분제 사회'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a system where a person's rank is decided by birth, so it mainly comes up in history classes and period dramas. Common uses are '신분제를 폐지하다' and '신분제 사회'.

examples.en: I got up at the first light of dawn and climbed the mountain.
The air at early dawn is very cold and clear.
My father went out to work from the break of dawn.
The streets at early dawn are very quiet.
A call came at the crack of dawn and I was startled.
I studied for the exam until the first light of dawn.

explain: 날이 막 밝아 오기 시작하는 이른 시각을 말해요. 그냥 '새벽'보다 글이나 이야기 속에서 분위기 있게 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It names the very early moment when daylight is just beginning to appear. It is a more atmospheric word than plain '새벽' and is common in writing and storytelling.

examples.en: In the Cenozoic era, mammals increased greatly.
Dinosaurs lived in the Mesozoic, not the Cenozoic.
Cenozoic fossils were found in this area.
The Cenozoic is an era that continues to the present.
The Paleozoic, Mesozoic and Cenozoic eras came up on the exam.
There was an ice age in the late Cenozoic.

explain: 지구의 역사를 나눈 '고생대, 중생대, 신생대' 중 마지막 시대로, 이 세 개를 한 묶음으로 외우는 경우가 많아요. 공룡은 중생대 이야기라서 헷갈리지 않게 조심하세요.
explain_en: It is the last of the three eras '고생대, 중생대, 신생대' in Earth's history, and people usually memorize them as a set. Dinosaurs belong to the Mesozoic, so be careful not to mix them up.

examples.ko: 주말에 집에서 쉬는 게 저한테는 신선놀음이에요.
examples.en: Resting at home on weekends is pure bliss to me.

examples.ko: 월급 받으면서 이렇게 노니 신선놀음이 따로 없어요.
examples.en: Getting paid while loafing like this, it couldn't be more carefree.

examples.ko: 신선놀음에 빠져 시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I got lost in leisurely fun and didn't notice the time.

examples.ko: 바둑 두며 보내는 오후가 신선놀음 같아요.
examples.en: An afternoon spent playing baduk feels like a carefree idyll.

examples.ko: 휴가 내내 신선놀음만 했더니 몸이 근질근질해요.
examples.en: I only lounged around the whole vacation, and now I'm itching to move.
If you keep lazing around like that, your work will pile up.

explain: 신선처럼 걱정 없이 편하게 노는 모습을 부러워하거나, 일은 안 하고 한가하다고 핀잔할 때 둘 다 써요. 어떤 뜻인지는 말투와 상황으로 알 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 게임에 빠져 하루가 다 갔어요, 신선놀음에 도낏자루 썩는 줄 모른다더니.
phrases.en: A whole day went by in the game, just like the saying about losing track of time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재미있는 일에 푹 빠지면 시간이 가는 줄 모른다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that when you are absorbed in something fun, you lose track of time.
phrases.en_equiv: Time flies when you're having fun

explain_en: It can express envy at someone carefree like an immortal sage, or tease someone for idling instead of working. Tone and situation tell you which meaning is intended.

examples.en: Human dignity is an inviolable value.
In that country, the king's authority was sacrosanct.

examples.ko: 이 규칙은 신성불가침이 아니니 바꿀 수 있어요.
examples.en: This rule isn't untouchable, so it can be changed.
I think privacy is a sacred area that must not be violated.

examples.ko: 법 앞에서는 어떤 권력도 신성불가침이 아니에요.
examples.en: Before the law, no power is above question.

examples.ko: 가족의 저녁 식사 시간은 우리 집에서 신성불가침이에요.
examples.en: Family dinner time is sacred in our house.

explain: 신성해서 누구도 건드리거나 침범하면 안 된다는 강한 말이에요. 진지한 글에도 쓰지만, 가족 식사 시간처럼 '절대 방해하면 안 되는 것'을 농담처럼 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is a strong word meaning something is so sacred that no one may touch or violate it. It appears in serious writing, but people also use it half-jokingly for things that must never be disturbed, like family mealtime.

examples.en: In Hinduism, cows are treated as sacred.
People in the past regarded big trees as sacred.

examples.ko: 그 부족은 산을 신성시하면서 함부로 오르지 않아요.
examples.en: That tribe holds the mountain sacred and doesn't climb it casually.
Some fans treat celebrities as almost sacred.
In some cultures, fire is also held sacred.
If you treat tradition as too sacred, change becomes hard.

explain: '~을 신성시하다'처럼 목적어에 조사 '을/를'을 붙여 써요. 실제 종교뿐 아니라 '전통을 신성시하다'처럼 지나치게 높이 받드는 느낌으로도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It takes an object marked with 을/를, as in '~을 신성시하다'. Besides religion, it can carry a sense of revering something excessively, as in '전통을 신성시하다'.

examples.en: My friend complains about his lot every time we meet.
Just lamenting your fate won't change anything.

examples.ko: 할머니는 옛날 일을 떠올리며 신세타령을 하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother recalled the old days and lamented her lot in life.
I couldn't find a job, so my self-pitying complaints increased.
Stop the sob story and let's look for a way together.
The lyrics of this song are sad like a lament over one's lot.

explain: 자기 처지가 불쌍하고 힘들다고 길게 늘어놓는 말을 가리켜요. '신세타령을 하다/늘어놓다'로 쓰고, 조금 지겹다는 느낌이 있어서 남에게 쓰면 핀잔처럼 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to going on at length about how pitiful and hard one's situation is. It is used as '신세타령을 하다/늘어놓다', and it can sound like a mild scolding when said about someone else.

examples.en: Despite the teacher's repeated pleas, the students came late.
I haven't forgotten my mother's earnest request.
After much earnest begging, I finally got a promise.

examples.ko: 친구는 비밀로 해 달라고 신신당부를 했어요.
examples.en: My friend earnestly begged me to keep it secret.
Even though I'd been told repeatedly, I made a mistake again.
Thanks to my father's repeated warnings, I went carefully.

explain: 몇 번이고 간곡하게 부탁하거나 당부하는 일이에요. '신신당부를 하다'처럼 쓰고, 보통 걱정되거나 꼭 지켜야 하는 일을 말할 때 나와요.
explain_en: It means asking or urging someone earnestly, again and again. It is used as '신신당부를 하다', typically about something worrying or something that must be kept.

examples.en: Mom earnestly urged me to be careful with fire.
I earnestly begged my friend to keep the secret.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 약을 거르지 말라고 신신당부해요.
examples.en: The doctor keeps urging me not to skip my medicine.

examples.ko: 출발 전에 조심하라고 신신당부하는 아버지가 생각나요.
examples.en: I remember my father earnestly telling me to be careful before leaving.
The team leader urged us over and over to keep the deadline.
I begged you so earnestly, and you forgot again?

explain: 그냥 '부탁하다'보다 걱정하는 마음으로 거듭 간곡하게 말한다는 느낌이 강해요. 윗사람이 하면 '신신당부하셨어요'처럼 높여 말해요.
explain_en: Compared with plain '부탁하다', it carries a stronger sense of repeated, earnest asking out of worry. When an elder does it, you say it respectfully, like '신신당부하셨어요'.
